correctness.rationale: The proof substitutes the standard complementary-modulus expansions of the complete elliptic integrals into the source paper's exact optimizer equation. The resulting singular equation is inverted on the W_{-1} branch and a mean-value estimate controls the asymptotic error. The sharp-constant deficit follows from the same expansion. The boundary L2 identity is an exact elementary integral, and its rate follows by substitution. Numerical checks against the exact elliptic equation support the constants but are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary source gives the exact finite-K characterization and qualitative K-to-infinity limits, but only quantifies the opposite K-to-1 endpoint. Targeted literature and SCOPE-archive searches did not locate the Lambert-W optimizer scale, the 1/(K^2 log K) deficit law, or the exact boundary L2 formula. Wegmann's 1993 full text was not independently inspected and remains the principal older-literature residual risk; unindexed concurrent work is also possible.

value.rationale: The result resolves the large-distortion scale left qualitative in the new extremal theorem, revealing a logarithmic flattening mechanism, a sharp deficit asymptotic, and a quantitative boundary-degeneration law connecting the elliptic extremals to the one-dimensional 4/pi extremal.
